- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots downward; apply a 2–5 day lag correction, smoothing the drop.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >2% from peak), model overreacts; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model underestimates further decline; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias for next 7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5–7 days are too high relative to recent history, apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–2% from first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 1.00), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
